Evelyn / Marcus —

Attached is a quick spreadsheet (CloudWave-MAP-v3-pricing.xlsx) with two lanes:

A) Firm commit ladder (best for predictable unit economics):
- Tier 1: $0–$250k (months 0–3) -> list price ($0 discount)
- Tier 2: $250k–$750k (months 4–9) -> 12% off list
- Tier 3: $750k–$2M (months 10–21) -> 20% off list + reserved throughput credits

We assume a 60/40 split hosted vs private-deploy billable mix for example math. The spreadsheet shows the monthly burn and breakpoints. Under a firm-commit model we include an early-exit true-up with a 90-day notice and pro-rated repayment schedule.

B) Usage-anchored ladder (easier for product-driven ramp):
- Gate 1: POC completion (>= 1k tokens/day median for 7 days) -> baseline
- Gate 2: Pilot ramp (>= 30% week-over-week token growth, sustained for 2 weeks) -> 10% discount applied retro to pilot start
- Gate 3: Production (>= 100k tokens/day sustained) -> 18% discount + option to convert to firm commit at capped effective price

Tradeoffs: firm commit -> better pricing but procurement/legal prefer usage-anchored. We can hybridize: convert usage gates into soft milestones that trigger temporary discounts, then convert to firm commit for an annual renewal.

Action items I can take before Wed call:
- Clean the spreadsheet math for the 60/40 mix.
- Draft two short bullets describing contract language for a usage-anchored true-up.

—Rishi
Director, Commercial Pricing
Redwood Inference
